response:
*looks up from magazine*

Yep. Scruffy's seen this boiler before.

*turns page*

## What We're Doin'

Kill the mainframe. That's it. Move the COBOL batch jobs to Java services on cheap VMs. Keep Oracle 11g—pay the vendor extortion for extended support another year. Fixes the CFO's $800K problem, buys time on the Oracle deadline.

## What We're NOT Doin'

Cloud-first. Microservices. The "transformation." Any of that. Scruffy's been around long enough to know when the boiler's too old to rebuild—you just keep it runnin' till you can afford a new one.

## Who's Gonna Be Mad

The CEO. Gonna have to tell him "cloud-first" ain't happenin' this year. Maybe next. *shrugs* Board's gonna hear "we stabilized operations and reduced costs 40%" instead. If that ain't good enough, well... Scruffy don't make the laws of physics.

The Head of Compliance gets her SOX fixes—that's the one that puts people in jail, so that one's non-negotiable. She'll be happy.

## Honest Probability

60% we pull this off. Failure looks like: batch jobs still broken in 8 months, mainframe contract auto-renews, we're back where we started plus $600K poorer.

## When to Walk Away

If those three COBOL developers won't cooperate. Can't move batch jobs we don't understand. Simple as that.

If that happens, Scruffy's recommendation is: don't do the project. Pay the $800K, keep the lights on, use the $1.8M to hire contractors to shadow those developers for a year and document everything. Boring. Expensive. Only thing that works.

## If They Proceed Anyway

*scratches head*

They should expect exactly what happened to the last architect. $1.2M spent, nothin' delivered, somebody gets fired. Probably me. Scruffy's survived worse.

Look, the real problem ain't technical. It's that everybody wants a miracle and nobody wants to pay for one. Scruffy's been fixin' boilers for 30 years—sometimes the boiler's fine, it's the building that's wrong.

*goes back to magazine*

Scruffy's on it. But Scruffy's also updatin' his resume.

Yep.
